findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits DB fallback and causes stale denies
findings.body: Check() checks permDenialCache first (line 117) and returns Allowed:false immediately on hit, without consulting the DB. The entry is set after a DB-backed deny (line 154) with shortCacheTTL (30s) and is never cleared when permissions are granted. So if a user is denied once and then granted access, all Checks for that namespace/user/action/name/parent are incorrectly denied until TTL expires. This reintroduces the exact staleness the PR claims to fix (creator/grant propagation) and defeats the new cachedPerms->DB fallback on lines 123-139, which is unreachable when a denial is cached.

findings.title: List serves stale cached permissions with no revalidation
findings.body: List() uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and, on hit, returns listPermission directly from the cached scope map with no DB fallback. Unlike Check(), which was changed to requery the DB when the cached map does not authorize the requested name, List has no way to detect staleness. Newly granted scopes (e.g. just-created dashboard/folder) will be missing from List results until permCache TTL (30s) expires, contradicting the PR goal of fetching newly created resources.

findings.title: DB fallback still uses stale cached folder tree
findings.body: Even when Check() falls back to getIdentityPermissions on a cached-permission miss, checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions calls buildFolderTree which returns the cached folderTree if present (shortCacheTTL 30s). A dashboard in a newly created folder, or a newly granted parent-folder permission, will still evaluate against the old tree and be denied. The PR refreshes permission scopes but never refreshes/invalidates folderCache, so inherited-permission checks remain stale.
